title: Customer Priority Gate & Engagement Playbook for Strategic Requests
creator: Liam O'Rourke
description: Create a standardized "priority gate" and engagement playbook that operationalizes how we accept, fast-track, or defer feature requests from strategic accounts. The deliverable is a lightweight decisioning flow + templated comms + escalation runbook that ties into the roadmap and Dedicated/Private capacity commitments. This playbook should reduce ad-hoc escalations, speed up TTR for VIP asks, and create clear handoffs between Sales/CS, PM, and Eng/RE to reduce unscoped work and unexpected SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page decision flow that defines inputs (impact signals, contract terms, technical feasibility) and outputs (R&D scope, timeline bucket, 'requires SOW')
Three templated email/slack responses for common outcomes (Accepted with ETA, Needs SOW, Deferred with alternatives)
Integration points documented with Roadmap board, Jira/Linear tags, and the Executive review cadence
Pilot with 3 active strategic accounts and feedback captured in post-pilot retro
SLA for initial response defined (e.g., 3 business days for triage and 15 business days for scoping)
notes: Initial hypothesis: ~40% of top-account escalations start from unclear acceptance criteria or lack of routing to the correct team (PM vs Solutions Eng).
Trade-offs discussed: keep the gate light-weight to avoid blocking valid urgent work vs. needing enough guardrails to prevent scope creep.
We will surface a 'fast lane' for security/compliance blockers that bypass standard timelines but require an approved emergency SOW.
Proposal to tag accepted items with 'vip-priority' and a TTL so items automatically re-evaluate each quarter.
